newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Stable in directionless, dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Stable in directionless, dull trade.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet in listless trade on Tuesday with traders searching for fresh direction.
"The market has been very dull recently. There is no news to inspire sentiment," said one trader.

Some Mideast and Mediterranean cargoes sailing eastward are expected to arrive in Singapore in the second half of June, easing the seasonally tight supplies in the summer season but also putting prices under pressure, traders said.
Traders said cargo owners may lower their offers later this week due to slack buying interest.
"There are fewer cargoes coming here than usual but demand is very poor," said one trader.

Despite the fact that Singapore weekly residue stocks for the week ending June 4 fell 465,000 barrels to 10.312 million barrels, one independent trader said he saw sufficient inventories in the short term.
A major said he was still taking term cargoes from the Mideast but the demand was just routine.
In the swaps market, June swaps were at $99.00/$99.75 per tonne and July swaps were at $99.00/$98.75.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is expected to annouce its tender award on Wednesday to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent fuel oil for lifting in the the first half of July.
In the sleepy SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, no transaction was reported on late Tuesday, with July contract bid/offered at $98.00/$99.00.
